title: How to organize the dining room sideboard surface
description:
Hold serving dishes during a meal and a small, deliberate display between them.

This is The Sideboard Surface in the Dining Room. About 15-30 min.

WHAT DONE LOOKS LIKE
A taped run of bare wood at the end nearest the table long enough for the roasting pan, three display objects grouped at the lamp end, no paper on the wood, and the lamp cord the only cord in sight.

THE SIX PASSES
Sort: Take everything off the wood, including the picture frames and the candlesticks, and give every piece of paper a verdict tonight: act on it, file it, or recycle it.
Straighten: Keep the end nearest the table entirely bare for setting dishes down, and group whatever display you keep at the far end near the lamp.
Shine: Lift each object rather than dusting around it, then work the wax drips off with a plastic card and gentle warmth, and treat the pale rings left by cold glasses.
Safety: Trace the lamp cord from the shade to the outlet and count everything else sharing that plug, because a sideboard collects a lamp, a charger, and a warming tray on one socket hidden behind heavy furniture nobody pulls out.
Standardize: The taped run stays bare, always, and the display group is three objects at most.
Sustain: Nothing sleeps on this wood overnight except the lamp and the three display pieces, so the last thing off it each night is whatever arrived that day, removed by whoever set it down.

THE STANDARD YOU LEAVE BEHIND
The taped serving run stays bare, three display objects at the far end, and no paper on the wood at any hour.
